# Overview

This vignette demonstrates multivariate seed–PPI using partial CCA (mCCA) in a searchlight-friendly way. The function `seed_ppi_mcca()` computes, for each neighborhood, the canonical association between a multivariate seed (seed set or seed time-series) and the local interaction block formed by the neighborhood time-series multiplied by the task design (PPI-style interactions). It:

- Works on matrices (`T x V`) or `neuroim2::NeuroVec` directly.
- Builds neighborhoods using `neuroim2::searchlight()` or accepts a precomputed list of integer index vectors.
- Optionally prewhitens via `fmriAR` and supports neural-domain deconvolution via `fmrihrf`.
- Returns a scalar map per center (first canonical correlation `r1` or a Wilks proxy) and optional canonical weight vectors for interpretability.

Dependencies:

- `neuroim2` (required for the searchlight/neuroim2 path)
- `fmriAR` and `fmrihrf` (optional; only when `prewhiten = TRUE` or `domain = "neural"`)

# Quick start (matrix with precomputed neighborhoods)

```r
library(multiPPI)
set.seed(1)
Tn <- 120
V  <- 200

# Synthetic data and a simple design
Y <- matrix(rnorm(Tn * V), Tn, V)
X <- cbind(1, task = rnorm(Tn))

# Seed as indices into columns of Y (e.g., a set of seed voxels)
seed_idx <- 1:8

# Precomputed neighborhoods: stride across columns, neighborhoods of ~12
neigh <- lapply(seq(1, V, by = 4), function(i) as.integer(intersect(i:(i+11), 1:V)))

sl <- seed_ppi_mcca(
  data          = Y,
  seed          = seed_idx,
  design        = X,
  nuisance      = NULL,
  neighborhoods = neigh,
  tr            = 1,
  domain        = "hemo",     # use "neural" + fmrihrf for deconvolved domain
  prewhiten     = FALSE,       # set TRUE + fmriAR to prewhiten
  pca           = list(seed_k = 5, light_k = 10, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE),
  reg           = list(l2_x = 0.1, l2_y = 0.1),
  stat          = "r1",
  inference     = list(method = "none"),
  return        = c("map","weights")
)

str(sl$stat)
```

The result `sl` is a list of class `mppi_sl` with fields:

- `stat`: numeric vector of length equal to the number of neighborhoods
- `centers`: integer centers (first index per neighborhood if not from neuroim2)
- `weights_x` / `weights_y`: optional canonical weights per neighborhood
- `neighborhoods`: integer index vectors per center

# Searchlight via neuroim2 (recommended)

The recommended workflow is to work with `neuroim2` objects. Build neighborhoods using `neuroim2::searchlight()` from a `NeuroVol` mask, and pass a `NeuroVec` for the data. The code below illustrates the flow. Replace the example volume paths with your data.

```r
library(neuroim2)
library(multiPPI)

# Example placeholders — replace with your actual files
# nv   <- neuroim2::readNeuroVec("sub-01_task.nii.gz")
# mask <- neuroim2::readVol("sub-01_mask.nii.gz")

# For illustration only (not run by default):
# neighborhoods are built internally from the mask using searchlight()

# task design (T x m); provide your own design matrix or fmridesign model
# X <- as.matrix(my_design)  # e.g., cbind(1, encode = ..., recall = ...)

# seed specification can be: integer indices into columns of nv, logical mask, labels, or a T x q matrix
# seed_idx <- which(mask != 0)[1:200]  # example seed as first 200 masked voxels

# sl <- seed_ppi_mcca(
#   data     = nv,
#   seed     = seed_idx,
#   design   = X,
#   nuisance = NULL,
#   mask     = mask,
#   searchlight = list(radius = 6, eager = TRUE, nonzero = TRUE),
#   tr       = neuroim2::tr(nv),
#   domain   = "neural",      # deconvolution via fmrihrf
#   prewhiten= TRUE,          # fmriAR prewhitening
#   pca      = list(seed_k = 5, light_k = 12, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE),
#   reg      = list(l2_x = 0.1, l2_y = 0.1),
#   stat     = "r1",
#   inference= list(method = "param")
# )

# sl$stat contains a scalar per searchlight center. You can map it back to a volume:
# out <- neuroim2::emptyVolumeLike(mask)
# out[sl$centers] <- sl$stat
# neuroim2::writeVol(out, "sub-01_seedPPI_mCCA_r1.nii.gz")
```

# Practical guidance

- Keep PCA-reduced dimensions modest relative to T (e.g., `seed_k` ~ 5–10; `light_k` ~ 10–15) and use small ridge penalties (`l2_x`, `l2_y`) for stability.
- Use `prewhiten = TRUE` if you plan to do permutations; otherwise consider block permutations to respect autocorrelation structure.
- For task PPI, center design columns and residualize the seed interaction against nuisance and the neighborhood time-series (`seed_ppi_mcca()` handles this internally).
- Use `stat = "r1"` for a simple, group-friendly scalar (Fisher z-transform across subjects). Use `stat = "wilks"` for a multi-root effect size: true Wilks is computed as `-sum(log(1 - rho_j^2))` over canonical roots.
- Limit roots with `wilks_k` if neighborhoods are large (e.g., `wilks_k = 3`), trading a slight loss in sensitivity for speed and stability. Parametric p-values use a Bartlett approximation with `df = sum_{j=1..k} (p-j+1)(q-j+1)`.
- Residualization uses QR (not a dense projector) to reduce memory and improve numerical stability. You may see a warning if effective DOF after partialling is low: reduce `seed_k`/`light_k` or increase `l2_x`/`l2_y`.

## Nuisance & Whitening

`seed_ppi_mcca()` allows you to align nuisance handling with the rest of multiPPI:

- `runs` and `center_by`: Provide a run vector and set `center_by = "run"` to demean design/nuisance columns within run (recommended for PPI-style interactions).
- Prewhitening: When `prewhiten = TRUE`, the function estimates an AR model on residuals of `Y` after projecting out `[D,N]` per run and applies the same whitening transform to both `Y` and `[D,N]`. This mirrors `mppi_fit_whitened()` so regression invariance and permutation validity are preserved.

Example (matrix path):

```r
set.seed(10)
Tn <- 160
runs <- c(rep(1L, 80), rep(2L, 80))
Y <- matrix(rnorm(Tn * 150), Tn, 150)
X <- cbind(1, task = rnorm(Tn))
neigh <- lapply(seq(1, 150, by = 6), function(i) as.integer(intersect(i:(i+11), 1:150)))

sl <- seed_ppi_mcca(
  data      = Y,
  seed      = 1:10,
  design    = X,
  neighborhoods = neigh,
  tr        = 1,
  runs      = runs,
  center_by = "run",
  prewhiten = TRUE,
  domain    = "hemo",
  pca       = list(seed_k = 6, light_k = 12, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE),
  reg       = list(l2_x = 0.1, l2_y = 0.1),
  stat      = "r1"
)
```
